look_here_first: FOLLOW ONE FLOWER STALK BACK TO ITS NODE. In Japanese honeysuckle, flowers are paired, two at a time, arising from LEAF AXILS along the shoot rather than a terminal whorl. The strongly two-lipped flowers start pale white and may age yellow. The mature berries turn dark/black (the others red).

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Evergreen to semievergreen twining vine with opposite distinct elliptic to ovate short-petiolate leaves and usually hairy young stems; common escaped/invasive Texas vine.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Opposite simple leaves with entire to near-entire margins; petiole lengths and fused terminal bracts vary by species.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Paired axillary flowers with long strongly two-lipped white fading-yellow corollas ~45–57 mm and projecting reproductive parts; not terminal condensed whorls.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Dark nearly black mature berries commonly ~6–8 mm, supporting Japanese honeysuckle compared with the two red-fruited native species.
